question: Can disconnectivity graphs of a neural network's loss landscape identify weights that remain conserved across low-loss funnels and thereby suggest an interpretable input pathway?

key_findings.claim: The proposed analysis groups local minima through transition states in a disconnectivity graph and labels a weight conserved when its across-minimum standard deviation within a group falls below a chosen threshold.
key_findings.evidence: The method section imports an energy-landscape funnel representation, removes permutation-equivalent minima, and defines conservation directly in parameter space rather than in functions or predictions.

key_findings.claim: On a small checkerboard classifier, conserved connections visually align with pathways used to separate the alternating two-dimensional regions.
key_findings.evidence: The one-hidden-layer network's minima are organized into funnels and the corresponding diagrams highlight connections whose weights vary little within the selected groups.

key_findings.claim: For anonymized credit-card fraud data reduced by PCA, three globally conserved outgoing weights are all associated with input coordinate 6; perturbing them reduces the best AUC from about 0.95 to about 0.76.
key_findings.evidence: The study uses a 0.01 conservation threshold and contrasts the selected three-weight perturbation with random three-weight perturbations of similar size, whose average AUC remains around 0.90.

key_findings.claim: The credit experiment identifies an anonymous PCA coordinate, not a human-semantic financial feature, and its perturbation result shows performance sensitivity rather than a causal explanation of individual predictions.
key_findings.evidence: The dataset's original variables are anonymized and transformed, while the validation changes selected parameters and measures aggregate AUC without a feature-level ground truth or prediction-specific explanation target.

key_findings.claim: Weight conservation is not implementation invariant: scaling and other continuous reparameterizations can change parameter variance while leaving the network function unchanged, beyond the permutation symmetry explicitly handled here.
key_findings.evidence: The procedure quotients hidden-unit permutations but defines importance using raw weight dispersion; no normalization or test covers positive-homogeneous rescaling, coordinate changes, or mode connectivity between sampled minima.

method.core_idea: Borrow funnel and conservation concepts from molecular energy landscapes to identify neural connections whose weights are stable across families of low-loss minima.
method.mechanism: Enumerate minima and connecting transition states for a small network, build a disconnectivity graph, merge permutation-equivalent solutions, group minima at funnel nodes, compute per-weight dispersion within each group, and perturb low-dispersion weights to test association with task performance.
assumptions: The sampled minima and transition states adequately represent the relevant loss landscape.
Low variance of a raw parameter across a funnel is a meaningful proxy for functional importance.
Hidden-unit permutation is the main parameter symmetry requiring quotienting.
A fixed conservation threshold transfers meaningfully across weights and problems.

techniques.role: Summarizes minima, transition barriers, and funnel organization of the loss landscape.
Avoids treating hidden-unit permutations as distinct invariant groups.
Selects allegedly conserved and important connections.
Tests whether selected connections disproportionately affect aggregate performance.

evaluations.setting: Two-dimensional checkerboard classification with a one-hidden-layer network
evaluations.metric: Qualitative agreement between landscape funnels, conserved connections, and the known decision structure
evaluations.result: Highlighted pathways are reported to correspond to the alternating-region classification mechanism.
evaluations.baseline: Visual inspection of the learned classifier and ungrouped minima

evaluations.metric: AUC after perturbing three selected weights
evaluations.result: Best AUC falls from roughly 0.95 to 0.76 when the three globally conserved weights tied to coordinate 6 are perturbed.
evaluations.baseline: Similar-magnitude perturbations of three random weights, averaging roughly 0.90 AUC

limitations: Only tiny one-hidden-layer networks and two binary classification datasets are studied.
Enumerating minima and transition states is computationally prohibitive for modern models.
The conservation threshold is manually chosen and lacks sensitivity analysis or uncertainty intervals.
The study handles permutation symmetry but not scaling and other function-preserving reparameterizations.
No repeated perturbation trials, statistical error bars, semantic feature ground truth, or comparison with established attribution methods is reported.
failure_modes: Incomplete landscape exploration can make a weight appear conserved simply because alternative funnels were missed.
Raw parameter scaling can change the conservation ranking without changing predictions.
Correlated weights may be individually variable while their joint function is stable, or individually conserved while functionally redundant.
A global AUC drop can reflect general network damage rather than an interpretable task-specific mechanism.
Different grouping heights or variance thresholds can select incompatible explanations.
reusable_insights: Treat explanations as properties of functions or equivalence classes, not unnormalized parameter coordinates.
Use landscape ensembles to measure explanation stability across minima, but validate against function-preserving symmetries.
Compare selected interventions with matched random, magnitude-based, gradient-based, and concept-based controls.
Report threshold sensitivity and uncertainty over landscape sampling before naming a connection conserved.
open_questions: Can conserved mechanisms be defined in activation or function space so they are invariant to reparameterization?
Can scalable mode-connectivity samples replace exhaustive transition-state searches in modern networks?
Do funnel-conserved subnetworks improve prediction-specific explanations beyond established attribution methods?
How stable are selected weights across datasets, optimizers, seeds, and conservation thresholds?
What ground-truth benchmark could distinguish causal mechanism discovery from generic performance sensitivity?

competitive_landscape.title: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Integrated Gradients attributes individual predictions in input space and explicitly requires implementation invariance; this work gives a global parameter-space interpretation across minima but does not satisfy that invariance.

competitive_landscape.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
competitive_landscape.difference: Adebayo et al. test whether saliency depends on learned parameters and data; the conserved-weight paper uses targeted perturbation but lacks comparable randomization, reparameterization, and explanation-ground-truth sanity checks.

competitive_landscape.title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. introduce filter normalization for comparable landscape visualizations at useful network scales; this paper instead enumerates minima and barriers, then attaches an interpretability claim to within-funnel weight variance.

competitive_landscape.title: Loss Surfaces, Mode Connectivity, and Fast Ensembling of DNNs
competitive_landscape.difference: Garipov et al. find low-loss curves connecting trained solutions and exploit them for ensembles; disconnectivity graphs emphasize finite barriers and conserved parameters, a framing whose conclusions depend on how paths and symmetries are sampled.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Molecular disconnectivity graphs and conserved weights provide a physics-inspired route to interpreting neural networks through their full loss landscape.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Two small experiments connect low within-funnel weight variance to visual structure or a larger AUC drop than random perturbations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The cross-domain analogy is interesting as an exploratory workshop idea, but the evidence is too small and parameterization-dependent to establish a general interpretability method; scalability and functional invariance are the decisive missing pieces.

reviewer_notes: Read all 6 extracted pages and audited the landscape construction, symmetry handling, threshold, both experiments, and perturbation claim. Attribution, sanity-check, normalized-landscape, and mode-connectivity competitors were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
